Hey all! I've been thinking about how we're going to start a gift exchange for this community. A couple of things come to mind: not everybody is religious, not everybody believes in Santa, and NOBODY wants a lame gift.

To keep things neutral I think we should call our gift exchange just that, a gift exchange. Or better yet, World Exchange Day. This way it sounds like everybody is included, which everybody is. Nobody will be referred to as elves or Santa (officially that is, but if you want to call yourself Santa, that's cool). By staying neutral nobody gets left out.

I've participated in two Secret Santa gift exchanges on Reddit and am participating in my first Arbitrary Day gift exchange this year. What I'v noticed in my experience is that a lot of people are there to take advantage of the system. Because Reddit has grown so much, I feel there are a lot more people looking for a free gift. One way we could solve this issue is by allowing only "older" users to participate. Now, of course many of us here come from Reddit who have participated in many gift exchanges and have never scammed the system. And many more will come once we kick off our first exchange. We could somehow allow those people to participate if we could verify their good history.

Perhaps we could request validation photos? Or is there a way they could link to their Secret Santa profile?

I have been the victim of a scam on Reddit's Secret Santa exchange and have been rematched. We should strongly consider rematching as one of our own features.

I also believe that anybody who scams the system deserves an immediate lifetime ban. For those who give horrible gifts (literally like random shit from your glove box), we should at least put their names on a "list" or possibly ban them. This goes the same for those who don't post their gifts.

I don't believe in tier grouping by how much one wants to spend. Instead I believe we should consider Reddit's credit tiering program. I also like their premium elf idea, where you have to pay a fee to participate. This will further ensure that nobody is getting scammed. However, this should by no means be the only way to participate. The gift exchange should remain free forever.

Earlier I mentioned the vast amount of people participating in Reddit's gift exchange. Maybe to curve the amount of growth of our exchanges, any knowledge of them should travel by word of mouth only. This means we shouldn't post what we're doing on social media (I know there's no way of enforcing this but we can at least try by ourselves). In fact, this could be an invite-only thing. Only those who have been validated through past exchanges either on Reddit or wherever else can join. All others will have to be a contributing member of Voat for some time before they can join.
